newsitem.title: UK: Aberdeen to outsource admin, fund accounting.
newsitem.headline: Aberdeen to outsource admin, fund accounting.

text.p: Aberdeen Asset Management Plc said on Monday it would outsource investment administration and fund accounting to Henderson Plc to focus on its core asset management business.

Announcing interim results to end-March, Aberdeen said the industry was becoming increasingly dependent on computer systems, and it expected the level of ongoing investment in systems development to accelerate.
"We have therefore decided to outsource the investment administration and fund accounting for all group clients to Henderson Plc," a statement said.

Aberdeen reported interim pre-tax profits down to 3.28 million sterling from 3.38 million a year earlier, but an increased dividend of 1.25 pence from 1.0. The higher dividend was partly the result of a disparity which arose between the 1996 interim and final payouts.
It said the outsourcing would have initial transitional costs but would make a positive contribution to group profitability from 1998.
"The need for systems development, which would otherwise have involved significant capital expenditure, will be largely eliminated as a result of this decision."
It said resources could now be allocated to client service, compliance, statistical and marketing functions.
Aberdeen said a decision to eliminate any element of double charging in its pricing structure had reduced income in the period, although it represented only a small proportion of total turnover.
Funds under management rose six percent in the period to 3.01 billion sterling despite the stronger pound's effect on the valuation of its international funds, it said.
